Erdos269.erdos_269.variants.rational.note: The FC 'rational' variant says the series is rational for every finite P with |P|>=2, so one irrational case refutes it; the disproof takes P={2,3}. Steve Fan proved on the erdosproblems.com forum (26 Jun 2026) that for |P|=2 the series factors as S1*S2 with (p-1)S1+(q-1)S2=p+q-1 and is transcendental (Hecke-Mahler series). The proof file itself credits Fan's factorisation and identity. Settled five months before PR #10603.

Erdos500.erdos_500.note: The FC statement is a 'question value' problem: cliqueExtremalNumber n 3 4 = erdos_500.answer, with the answer left as sorry. The proof sets OMA.answer := K4Count.value, an inclusion-exclusion sum over all subsets of the 4-sets of Fin n, and proves it equals the extremal number. That only restates the definition as a brute-force finite count; it says nothing about ex_3(n,K_4^3) (Turan's 5/9 conjecture is untouched). It exploits the open answer slot, so it is not a solution of Erdos 500.

erdos-1054.note: The statement conjoins (i) f(n)<=eps*n on a density-1 set for every eps>0 and (ii) limsup f(n)/n=infinity; the disproof refutes (i). erdosproblems.com/1054 records that Tao (comments to #468) proved the upper density of {n: f(n)<=delta n} is << delta^2, which already makes (i) false for small delta. The statement file itself quotes Tao's bound, and the proof formalizes Tao's second-moment bound plus Romanoff. So the result was known before PR #11542.

erdos-521.note: The proof's own header says 'That the almost-sure statement fails is known'. On the erdosproblems.com forum (Apr 2026), Kovac posted a write-up, built on Letwin's and Tao's ideas, of a disproof of a.s. convergence R_n/log n -> 2/pi for Rademacher coefficients (Corollary 1.4 of the write-up). The Lean argument is a different route to the same known negative answer.

mo-136792.note: The statement matches the question: standard Borel spaces as Polish spaces, K analytic, g Borel, h measurable for sigma(analytic sets), (x,y) in K with g(x,y)=h(x) for every x; is there an analytically measurable lift f? The disproof builds a counterexample by a diagonal argument over well-founded Borel codes for sigma(Sigma^1_1) sets. The MO question (2013) has 0 answers; George Lowther only guessed 'no' in a comment. I found no published counterexample, but this could be folklore descriptive set theory, so an expert check is advisable.

mo-200855.note: The formal statement is the asker's conjecture word for word: symmetric 0/1 adjacency with zero diagonal, g12=g13=1, g23=0, 0<lambda<1/(n-1), y1>=y2 and y1>=y3 imply x1/y1 > y3/z3, where x and z are the Katz-type scores after deleting 12 and adding 23. The question (2015) has no answers, and the asker checked n<=8 only. The disproof gives an explicit 15-vertex graph at t=1/30, with the scores computed exactly from integer solutions. The disproof is a finite counterexample check.

mo-236533.note: The statement asks for a row-stochastic X with AX having equal diagonal entries that dominate their rows. A 2016 comment on the question already observes that X_ij = 1/n works: every entry of AX is 1/n. The proof uses this trivial matrix. Answered on the page itself.

mo-270743.note: The statement is that keeping the s rows of largest energy minimizes ||A - A_S||_F^2. The two 2017 MO answers already prove exactly this: the error is the sum of the squared norms of the dropped rows.

mo-352184.note: The formal statement ('every score-class contains a fair-indexed tournament') is the natural reading of the 2020 question, which has 0 answers. The comment-thread counterexamples (22225555 and others) concern stronger variants or monotone orderings, not the question itself. The disproof is an exhaustive kernel search: for n=16, no fair-indexed tournament has scores 3^4 9^12, and a tournament with those scores exists. This genuinely answers the question (no), and it is a finite check.

mo-429559.note: F[a,b]=F(a,b) implies a and b are algebraic. Wojowu's comment on the question (Sep 2022), accepted by the asker, settles this: it is Zariski's lemma, a finitely generated algebra that is a field is a finite extension. Classical.

mo-479301.note: The statement (q-log-convexity of S^m_n for every m>=2) is faithful. The disproof uses m=5, n=7, coefficient of q^2. That is exactly the counterexample in the MO answer of 24 Jul 2026 (coefficient -499140), posted months before PR #9144.

mo-515455.note: The statement asks for nonzero integers with a^4+b^4+c^4+d^4=(a+64b+64c+64d)^4. The proof plugs in the 24-digit solution from the accepted MO answer (Oct 2026), and the proof comment says so.

oeis-a000122.note: The statement says sum_k a(k)e^{-k pi} = theta_3(e^{-pi}) = pi^{1/4}/Gamma(3/4), and the definition of a matches the entry. Plouffe's 2025 'conjecture' is the classical special value of the Jacobi theta function at q=e^{-pi} (Ramanujan, Borwein-Borwein; listed among theta special values). Known long before PR #12190.

oeis-a000332.note: Adamson's family is x*prod_i (1+x^{b^i}+...+x^{(b-1)b^i})^5 = x/(1-x)^5 for every base b>=2, stated as a coefficientwise limit. The product without the 5th power is 1/(1-x) by uniqueness of base-b digits (a classical identity), so the claim is immediate. The formal statement is faithful. The entry's displayed '1,5,14' is a typo for 1,5,15, as the statement file notes.

oeis-a001936.note: The statement a(n) == a(9n+2) (mod 4) is faithful (convolution square of 4-regular partition counts). It was settled before: the entry has Somos's 2012 formula a(9n+2) = a(n) + 4*A210656(3n), which gives the congruence at once (A210656 is an eta-quotient). Independently, Zaimi's proof (cited in MO 59192) that a(n) == sigma(4n+1) (mod 4), together with sigma(9m) == sigma(m) (mod 4), gives it in two lines.

oeis-a002735.note: Mathar's a(2n+1)=4a(2n). The entry records 'Mathar's conjecture is true' with a proof by Sela Fried, 8 Dec 2025, and the statement file says so.

oeis-a003625.note: Provvedi's 2018 conjecture: X^2+X+2 is irreducible over GF(p) iff p == 3,5,6 (mod 7). The statement is faithful. This is the textbook quadratic-reciprocity fact for discriminant -7. formal-conjectures (OeisA3625.conjecture, at the pinned commit) already marks it 'research solved', notes the equivalence is classical, and links a public Lean proof by KitaKen1. Known before PR #13124.

oeis-a007953.note: Marcus's digit-insertion rank identity. The statement file itself says 'Sela Fried proved this in 2025' (A007953/a007953.pdf, Theorem 1).

oeis-a010905.note: Barker's recurrence a(n)=4a(n-1)-a(n-2) for the Pisot sequence E(4,15). The entry (and the statement file) record Sloane's 2016 proof with the PtoRv program of Ekhad-Sloane-Zeilberger.

oeis-a025755.note: Mathar's 2014 recurrence. The statement file says Robert Israel confirmed it (Oct 2014) for n>=2. That is the corrected range stated here.

oeis-a028886.note: Kurkov's criterion (Dec 2025): (2m+1)^2-8 is prime iff q(m+1)+C(q,2)+1 is never a square for 1<=q<=2(m-2); the formal statement is exact. Setting X=2q+2m+1 turns the square condition into N=X^2-8s^2, so the claim is that N is composite iff it has a second representation by x^2-8y^2 in a range. The proof does genuine arithmetic in Z[sqrt2] (Euclidean division, norms, factor splitting). No earlier proof found; the entry still lists it as a conjecture.

oeis-a037958.note: Mathar's recurrence. The entry marks it 'verified by Robert Israel (Jun 28 2018)', as the statement file notes.

oeis-a047872.note: McEachen's 2021 conjecture: a(n)=floor(|B(2n+2)/B(2n)|) = floor((n+1)(2n+1)/(2 pi^2)). The statement is faithful. The ratio equals x_n*zeta(2n+2)/zeta(2n) with x_n=(n+1)(2n+1)/(2pi^2), so the claim needs frac(x_n) to exceed about n^2 4^{-n}. The proof checks n<2048 by interval bounds and handles large n with an explicit Beukers-integral irrationality-measure bound for pi^2 (Hanson lcm bound). That is a substantive argument. The entry still says 'conjectured', and I found no earlier proof.

oeis-a051064.note: Mathar's 2025 note '[Lengyel?]' is right: T. Lengyel, 'The order of the Fibonacci and Lucas numbers', Fibonacci Quart. 33 (1995) 234-239, proved v_3(F_n) = v_3(n)+1 if 4|n and 0 otherwise. That is exactly both conjuncts (v_3(F_4n) = v_3(3n), and the other quadrisections are 0). A classical result.

oeis-a052183.note: Mathar's 2012 three-term recurrence for (n+2)C(3n,n)/(2n+1). The statement is faithful (shifted to n=t+2). The proof is a factorial-ratio identity checked by field_simp/ring. Routine holonomic identity, not otherwise verified in the entry.

oeis-a056084.note: The entry says the formula a(n)=(1458n-729+(-1)^n*725)/4 was 'conjectured by Weidmann, explained by Robert Israel, Apr 13 2015' (k^8 == 1 mod 729 iff k == +-1, since the group is cyclic of order 486).

oeis-a061062.note: The Kurepa-like claim 'p does not divide a(p-1) for primes p>3' was already refuted in the entry by T. D. Noe (Dec 2004) with p=20879. The disproof verifies that same witness.

oeis-a071284.note: Barker's period-10 conjecture for the denominators of the order-4 Peirce sequence. I simulated the formal insertion model, and it reproduces the entry's example rows for orders 1-5 (e.g. order 4: 2,4,3,1,4,3,4,2,...), so the encoding is faithful. Periodicity follows from the translation-invariant insertion rule. Routine.

oeis-a072872.note: Cloitre's 2002 conjecture: a(n) < prime(n) for n>47, where a(n) is the least k>0 with n | 2^k-k. The disproof shows no k<=65000 works for n=6298, while prime(6298)=62753<65000 (kernel-checked prime count). I recomputed a(6298)=77742 > 62753; it is the first counterexample, and the b-file stops at n=1000. A genuine refutation by finite search.

oeis-a081071.note: Ratushnyak's identity. The entry records 'The above conjecture is true for n >= 1' (Nguyen Tuan Anh, Aug 2 2025), quoted in the statement file.

oeis-a084044.note: The 2003 conjecture a(n)=0 iff 10|n, where a(n) is the least palindromic multiple of n containing n as a substring. The formalization is faithful (digit lists, substring anywhere). The 'if' direction is trivial. The 'only if' direction is a short elementary construction: repeat a palindromic block containing n, using periodicity modulo the part of n coprime to 10. No earlier proof found; the entry and the sibling A084043 still call it a conjecture.

oeis-a087403.note: The conjecture 'no term is zero' is already refuted in the entry ('The conjecture is not true...', Farideh Firoozbakht, 2015), as the statement file says. The disproof uses n=100.

oeis-a092674.note: Perry's 2004 conjecture that the constant terms are never negative. The polynomials are linear in X: the X-coefficient B satisfies sum_{i<=n} B(i)floor(n/i) = [n=1], so B(n) = mu(n) - mu(n/2), and the constant term is phi(n) - mu(n) + mu(n/2) >= 0 (this matches the data 0,3,3,1,5,0,...). Routine.

oeis-a098746.note: Burstein's 2017 conjecture: |Av_n(4231,42513)| = |Av_n(1342,13254)|. The formal statement compares the two pattern-avoidance counts directly, with the occurrence definition correct and n=0 included. {1342,13254} is not a symmetry of {4231,42513}, so this is a nontrivial Wilf-equivalence. The 3900-line proof works through skew-sum decompositions. Albert et al. (2004) enumerated only the first class, and I found no earlier proof of the equivalence.

oeis-a102827.note: Van der Sanden's conjecture: in every base the 'True already' sequence has no term divisible by the base. The formal definition follows the entry: least positive x whose last digit d has been written exactly floor(x/b) times so far, with no monotonicity required. I simulated it independently: it matches the data and Mathar's a(99)=212, and gives a(332)=20 right after a(331)=1002 creates the first two zeros. Genuine counterexample in base 10, finite check; no earlier report found.

oeis-a111108.note: The entry already says 'The conjecture follows from the formula A001333(n) = ((1-sqrt2)^n+(1+sqrt2)^n)/2' (Max Alekseyev, Oct 2005).

oeis-a113249.note: Dement's conjecture that a(m,2n+1) is a perfect square for every m is faithfully stated. But KitaKen1's public Lean repo 'oeis-a113249-family-square-terms-lean' already proves it as one parameterised theorem for the whole family (p = m^2, odd terms are y_p(n)^2 for a second-order y_p). formal-conjectures, at the commit this site pins, marks A113250/A113252/A113255 'research solved' with a link to that proof. The site's proof uses the same idea (odd terms are squares of a second-order sequence). Known before PR #7849.

oeis-a122554.note: Mathar's two 2009 conjectures. The entry reports both proved by Sela Fried (Feb 2026), and the statement file says 'This file states the known result'.

oeis-a127628.note: Mathar's 2011 recurrence. The entry marks it 'verified by Robert Israel, Aug 28 2020', as the statement file notes.

oeis-a132304.note: Bala's Aug 2025 conjecture: a(np^k) == a(np^{k-1}) (mod p^{2k}) for primes p>=5 and n,k>=1, where a(n) = sum_k T(n,k)^4 over trinomial coefficients. The statement is exact. The 690-line proof is a genuine supercongruence argument: it clears denominators in binomial and multiset-binomial products, pairs i with pj-i, uses (1+x+x^2)=(1-x^3)/(1-x), and the fourth power kills off-grid terms. The entry still lists it as a conjecture; the nearest literature (Otmani-Belbachir 2025, central trinomial supercongruences) does not cover it. The proof notes that the cube case A132303 was done earlier by @rbajaj5 on GitHub.

oeis-a136050.note: Dale's 2016 conjecture: for twin primes (p,p+2) with p != 3, the digit sum of p(p+2) is == -1 (mod 9). The statement is faithful. It is immediate: p(p+2) = (p+1)^2-1 with 6 | p+1, so p(p+2) == -1 (mod 9), and the digit sum is congruent mod 9.

oeis-a151341.note: Mathar's 2017 recurrence for a(n) = Catalan(n)*Motzkin(n). The statement defines a by that product, which the entry lists as a (non-conjectural) formula, and proves the three-term P-recursive identity. Routine holonomic identity.

oeis-a158233.note: Curtz's 2009 conjecture that the terms lie in {0,3,4,6}. The triangle reading and offsets match the entry's controls (I recomputed 20000 terms: values {0,3,4,6}). The proof is a residue-class analysis of (m^2-n^2) products mod 9. Routine.

oeis-a165640.note: Layman's floor formula for the multisets of -2, 1, 3 with n members and sum 3. The statement counts the multiplicity triples exactly. Solving the two linear equations reduces this to a lattice-point count, so the formula is routine.

oeis-a174349.note: The conjecture that every i>=2 occurs in the array. The entry itself says it is 'obviously true: the integer i appears in row (prime(i+1)-prime(i))/2'.

oeis-a178297.note: Mathar's 2010 closed form 2a(n) = 11^n + 5*9^n - 6*7^n for collinear 6-subsets of {0..6}^n. The statement counts 6-sets whose real images are collinear. The formula follows from classifying grid lines with 6 or 7 points by coordinate patterns (constant, increasing or decreasing) and checks against the data. A routine but careful count (836-line proof); no earlier proof found.

oeis-a182025.note: Mathar's 2012 recurrence for 31C(2n,n-4) + sum C(2n,n-4-i)(4+i). The statement handles n<4 explicitly, as in the data. A routine holonomic (Zeilberger-type) identity.

oeis-a182883.note: Both parts (Bala's binomial-sum formula and the D-finite recurrence) are recorded as proved in the entry: Bala, Feb 7 2017, 'thus proving the above conjecture'.

oeis-a191625.note: Mathar's 2017 order-9 recurrence for two-sided prudent walks ending at the NE corner. The formal walk definition (prudent ray condition, top-or-right prefixes, final corner) matches Bousquet-Melou's. The entry gives Bousquet-Melou's proven algebraic g.f., and the recurrence follows from it mechanically. The 2100-line proof re-derives the kernel equation. Routine consequence of a known g.f.

oeis-a192473.note: Barker's recurrence for the x-coefficient of 1+x^n+x^{2n+2} mod x^2-x-1. Since x^k reduces to F_k x + F_{k-1}, this is a Fibonacci identity. Routine.

oeis-a192940.note: Mathar's recurrence for the x-coefficient of (x+2)(x+4)...(x+2n) mod x^2-x-1. It follows by multiplying the reduced pair by (x+2n) at each step. Routine.

oeis-a195915.note: Adams-Watters's observation T(2^j+n, 2^j+k) = T(n,k) for 2^j>n. The 0-based column indices and the bound k<n translate the 1-based source correctly. A 30-line XOR/Pascal-mod-2 induction. Routine.

oeis-a203232.note: Mathar's recurrence a(n)=12a(n-2)-36a(n-4) and g.f. for the (n-1)-st elementary symmetric function of (2,3,2,3,...). Routine.

oeis-a216211.note: Barker's 2017 rational g.f. (and order-12 recurrence) for self-avoiding walks from NW to SW corner in an n x 4 grid. The walk definition matches the data, including count(1)=1. The proof is a finite transfer-matrix computation. Routine.

oeis-a223906.note: Barker's closed form a(n)=2^{n+1}+3^{n+1}+4^n and g.f. With |s(3,1)|,|s(3,2)|,|s(3,3)| = 2,3,1 it is immediate from the defining sum. Routine.

oeis-a233398.note: Dale's 2025 conjecture n^n mod 3^n = 0 when 3|n. Trivial: (3y)^{3y} = 3^{3y} y^{3y}. A 3-line proof.

oeis-a242932.note: The A016742 claim is recorded as proved in the entry: Sela Fried, Mar 27 2026, characterizes the terms as {p+1, 2p, p(p+1)}, 'In particular, the conjecture regarding A016742 is true', quoted in the statement file.

oeis-a247250.note: Chen's 2014 conjecture that every Pell number P_n, n>1, has a primitive prime divisor. The statement file itself notes that Faye and Luca identify this as known: it follows from Carmichael's theorem on Lucas sequences (no exceptions for Pell).

oeis-a248521.note: Kotesovec's 2014 conjecture a(n) ~ pi n/2. The formal statement is the source condition (Nat.nth enumerator, ratio -> pi/2). Since cot(pi/(2k)) = 2k/pi + O(1/k) has increments below 1, the number of selected k <= K is the floor at K+1, about 2K/pi. Routine asymptotics.

oeis-a257838.note: Mathar's 2015 recurrence for the diagonal of iterated Fibonacci partial sums. The indexing is shifted correctly. Routine holonomic identity.

oeis-a262009.note: Hanna's 2015 conjectures on the 2-adic valuation of sum_{d|n} 2^{d^2}(n/d)^2. The d=1 term has valuation 2v_2(n)+1, strictly smaller than every other term, which gives both claims at once. Routine.

oeis-a266249.note: Barker's closed form, recurrence and g.f. for the ON cells of Rule 9. The conventions follow the entry's Mathematica program (background updated, cells -n..n) and reproduce the data. An eventually periodic pattern proved by induction. Routine.

oeis-a266607.note: Barker's recurrence and g.f. for the Rule 39 row values. The conventions follow the entry's program and reproduce the controls. Routine pattern induction.

oeis-a267262.note: Barker's closed form, recurrence and g.f. for the cumulative OFF cells of Rule 111. The conventions follow the program, and the controls match. Routine.

oeis-a267774.note: Barker's recurrence and g.f. for the Rule 207 row values. The conventions follow the program, and the controls match. Routine.

oeis-a273446.note: Blomberg's 2016 conjectures: Rule 729 gives the same counts as Rule 721 at stages 2^n-1, and a(n)=4*4^n-4*2^n for n>2. The outer-totalistic convention and the central-square count follow the program (controls 1,4,41). A routine pattern induction for a 2D CA.

oeis-a283648.note: Barker's g.f., parity closed forms and recurrence for the Rule 705 x-axis. The conventions follow the program, and the controls match. Routine.

oeis-a294513.note: Lang's 2017 conjecture a(n) = 2*A250327(n+1)/(n+1). The statement is faithful (computed in Q, A250327 as the numerator of the harmonic mean of pentagonal numbers). I recomputed it independently: it holds for n<1891 and fails at n=1891 (1892 = 4*11*43, and the RHS is not an integer: a leftover factor 1/11). A genuine counterexample by finite computation; not noted in the entry.

oeis-a303647.note: Barker's 2018 recurrence and g.f., plus the corrected (Sep 2026) A301483/A195350/A195339 identity, for a(n) = ceil(a(n-1)/(2^{1/3}-1)+1). r=1/(2^{1/3}-1) is a cubic Pisot number (r^3-3r^2-3r-1=0). The proof uses the standard model-sequence and error-bound argument. Routine Pisot-type argument.

oeis-a325695.note: Barker's recurrence and g.f. for strict 3-part partitions whose largest part is not the sum of the other two. A quasi-polynomial lattice-point count. Routine.

oeis-a329227.note: Barker's g.f. for products of consecutive Padovan numbers. Routine linear-recurrence identity.

oeis-a333686.note: Manyama's conjectured g.f. and recurrence for self-avoiding paths in a (2n+1) x 3 grid through the centre. The walk definition matches the data. The 3400-line proof is a 5-state transfer-matrix argument. Routine in method.

oeis-a337951.note: Hanna's mod-5 congruences for 4^{n(n-1)/2}+4^{n(n+1)/2}. Immediate from 4 == -1 (mod 5) and the parity of triangular numbers. Routine.

oeis-a350900.note: Schulte's 2022 conjectures: sum_{i,k<=n} f(gcd(i,n)/gcd(gcd(i,k),n)) = (f*phi) Dirichlet-convolved with A057660, multiplicativity, and the row-sum case. The statement is faithful (arbitrary f : N -> C). A standard gcd-sum and Dirichlet-convolution manipulation. Routine.

oeis-a364906.note: Wiseman's 2023 conjecture that the positions of 1 are exactly A319319. The counterexample is n=1547=7*13*17, with prime indices {4,6,7}: 4x+6y+7z=17 has the unique solution (1,1,1), so a(1547)=1. But the divisors 119 and 221 both have index-GCD 1, so 1547 is not in A319319. I checked this by hand. A finite counterexample.

oeis-a370261.note: Bala's 2024 integrality conjecture for sqrt(A370259(2n)/(n+1)). From T_{2n}(x)-1 = 2(x^2-1)U_{n-1}(x)^2 with x=2n+1, the quantity is (U_{n-1}(2n+1)/n)^2, and n | U_{n-1}(2n+1) because U_{n-1}(1)=n. Routine Chebyshev identity.

oeis-a374192.note: Detlefs's 2024 conjecture that the modified Collatz map reaches 1 or 10. The step function matches. The proof is a 40-line strong induction: two to four steps always give a smaller value. Routine.

oeis-a382437.note: The binomial-sum formula for a(n)=a(n-1)^2+4a(n-1), a(0)=2. Here a(n)+2 = 2T_{2^n}(2), and the sum is the standard expansion of 2T_m(1+y/2)-2 at y=2. Routine.

oeis-a383702.note: Mathar's 2025 recurrence for the x^2 coefficient of prod (x+4j+3). Routine holonomic identity.

oeis-a387426.note: Scheller's 2025 conjecture: every prime is in the sequence, and no composite k>24 is. The formal definition reproduces the data (I checked k<120). The proof is short and elementary. For a prime p, equal fractions force a*b*(q1-q2) = 2p(b-a), which is impossible. For a composite k>24 it gives explicit colliding pairs: (2A, 2Ax) with both fractions 1/2, (3B, 12B), and (5, 30) for k=36 and k=72. No earlier proof found.

oeis-a400127.note: Finiteness of a(n). The entry contains Rabahy's own proof (Oct 4 2026): a de Bruijn word occurs as the leading bits of some 3^k by density of k log_2 3. The statement file says so.

wp-generalized-star-height-problem.note: The proof file says 'Not an independent solution': it is OpenAI's published Lean proof (openai/math, 'Generalized Star Height at Most Three', 2026), concatenated and adapted. The statement is also adapted from OpenAI's. Known prior work.

The PR was opened 2026-11-27, four months later. The formal statement matches the erdosproblems wording, but the result was already public, so this is a port, not a new solution.

Erdos507.erdos_507.lower.note: The proof header credits OpenAI's github.com/openai/math (family 191, 'A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound', preprint dated 2026-09-25, in the repo since 2026-10-06), ported earlier in PR #9653 for Green 77. The answer chosen is n^c/n^2, which is an immediate consequence of that published construction. The statement is a 'question value' placeholder (any function between lowerBest and alpha), so even the target is only 'some improvement over KPS82'.

wpc-crouzeix-conjecture.note: The statement and the proof both say they are adapted from OpenAI math, DirectCrouzeix (item 325, 'The complete Crouzeix conjecture', preprints dated Sept 2026, Lean files present since the repo's first commit 2026-10-06). The PR (opened 2026-11-27) only adds a scalar transfer and the standard 2x2 sharpness example. The formal statement is faithful, but the result was already public.

erdos-1112.note: The formal statement asserts the affirmative answer for ALL 1<=d1<d2, k>=3. The PR disproves it with (d1,d2,k)=(1,2,3), a trivial case (gaps 1 or 2 make 3A cover all large integers of one parity, so 3A meets B). The universal claim was already refuted: Bollobas-Hegyvari-Jin 1997 (r_3(2,3) does not exist, on the problem page). Johan Land's Lean-checked dichotomy (r_k exists iff d2 >= k+1, July 2026, checked by T. Bloom on the forum) settles the whole problem.

mo-239436.note: The statement (surjectivity for all n>=1) is disproved at n=3 with c = t + t^3. The 2016 MO answer already proves F is not onto for n=3 via the invariant 12c0c4 - 3c1c3 + c2^2 >= 0, which is -3 for this c. So the disproof was already on MO.

mo-273966.note: Choosing the k items with largest v_i - w_i is optimal, a one-line exchange argument. This answer was already given in a comment on the question ('The common sense solution ... works'). Routine and already settled on the page.

mo-450392.note: The asker already proves the identity floor(sum_{h=0}^{2n+1} sqrt(n^2+h)) = 2n^2+3n+1 in the question body (Taylor bounds), and only asks for a more intuitive explanation. The formal statement is the identity itself, which was not open.

erdos-550.note: This is a disproof that exploits the formalization. The statement takes 'm_1<=...<=m_k and n sufficiently large' to mean one threshold M with M<=m_1 and M<=n, so the largest class m_k can be arbitrarily larger than n and m_1, m_2. The disproof takes classes (a,a,b) with b huge: R(T,G) >= |V(G)| = 2a+b, while the right side does not depend on b. That is not the EFRS85 regime, where n is large relative to the class sizes. E. Li claimed an affirmative proof in June 2026 [Li26], discussed on the forum.

mo-202165.note: The statement encodes Propp's relation faithfully on Z. Pieces are binned by the left endpoint of a window of width r, which is harmless since each site has finite mass. Equal mass and equal first moment is the same as equal mass and equal centre of mass. The proof establishes transitivity (with width 12(max r t + 1)) by a non-trivial prefix/blend construction. On MO, Propp thought the relation was not transitive and C. Remling's attempted proof was withdrawn as imprecise. No earlier solution was found.

mo-363072.note: The statement matches the revised MO question: A has zero line sums, is >=0 on the graph of sigma and <=0 off it, B is doubly stochastic and sigma maximises B's assignment sum, conclusion <A,B>_F >= 0. The proof is a short but non-obvious Birkhoff-von Neumann trick: S = P_sigma - A/m is doubly stochastic for m = 1 + sum A_{i,sigma(i)}, so <A,B> = m(<P_sigma,B> - <S,B>) >= 0. The question had no answers in six years. A correct, new, short argument.

mo-481044.note: The statement asks for a smooth, Z^d-periodic, divergence-free solution of u_t + (u.grad)u = 0 with non-zero time derivative, for each d>=2. The proof uses u = (sin(2 pi (x_2 - t)), 1, 0, ...), a Galilean boost of a stationary shear flow. Pressureless travelling shear waves of exactly this form, (c + n^{-s} cos(n x_2 - t), c), are the standard explicit solutions in the Himonas-Misiolek non-uniform-dependence literature (e.g. arXiv:1911.04405). The question is a request for examples, answered by a textbook construction.

mo-138395.note: The statement is the classical inequality alpha H(X) + (1-alpha) H(Y) >= K^2 H(Z) for all n and alpha in [0,1]. It adds the hypothesis K>0, which the question needs for Z to be a probability measure, and uses rpow conventions that only matter at alpha in {0,1}. Only alpha=1/2 (fedja, MO 138275) was proved before. The two answers to 138395 are not proofs. The 65 KB proof (reduction to three atoms, then a binary log-odds convexity argument) is substantive. The quantum, non-commuting extension asked at the end of the question is not covered.

mse-199784.note: The statement matches the question: m,n>1, all entries +-1, no non-trivial row/column permutation pair fixes A, and a unique Nash equilibrium that is fully mixed. Excluding the 1x1 case only strengthens the claim. The proof gives an explicit symmetric 7x7 +-1 matrix with equilibrium weights (i+1)/28. A is invertible, which gives uniqueness, and the distinct weights force total asymmetry. The 2012 question had no answers (a comment ruled out 4xn and 5x5). An explicit witness checked by finite computation; the open part was finding it.

oeis-a000126.note: The statement file itself says the conjecture was proved by Sela Fried (Feb 18, 2026, linked PDF). The OEIS entry says 'Layman's conjecture is true (see Fried link)'. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a000364.note: This is a disproof of Bala's pure-periodicity conjecture (modulus 27: a(1) != a(19) mod 27 while phi(27)=18). The statement file itself cites the published trureturing counterexample modulo 27, whose dossier dates the search to 2026-09-09. Already refuted before the PR.

oeis-a002050.note: Bala's conjecture: a(n) mod m is eventually periodic with period dividing phi(m). Since a(n) = A000629(n) - 1 = 2*A000670(n) - 1 for n>=1, it follows at once from Barsky's congruence A000670(n) == A000670(n+(p-1)p^(h-1)) (mod p^h) for n>=h, recorded in A000670. That gives eventual period phi(p^h) for each prime power, and the lcm divides phi(m). The PR gives an independent elementary proof of an already-implied fact.

oeis-a002742.note: The statement faithfully encodes the e.g.f. (2x/(1-x^2) + log(1-x^2)) e^{-x} and both of Bala's congruences (2k | a(n+2k) - a(n), (2k+1) | a(n+2k+1) + a(n)). The proof rewrites a(n) as a signed binomial transform of explicit factorial weights and uses standard binomial-sum divisibility. No prior proof found; elementary and short.

oeis-a005148.note: The statement file says 'Known proof: Miquel Cerda' (Zenodo, published 2026-11-03). The OEIS entry says '[This conjecture is true; see the Formula section and the Cerda link]'. Settled before the PR (opened 2026-11-27).

oeis-a008485.note: The statement matches Bala's supercongruence a(p) == p+1 (mod p^2) for primes p>=3, with a(n) = [x^n] Prod_{k<=n} (1-x^k)^{-n} (factors with k>n do not matter). The proof is a clean mod-p^2 power-series argument: (1-x)^p, (1-x^p)^p and (1-x^k)^p are 'good' up to degree p, then inversion. No earlier proof found in the entry or the literature searched. Elementary but genuine.

oeis-a016789.note: The formalized conjecture (Detlefs: y is a term iff y^3 == 2 mod 3) is marked true in the entry by Sela Fried (Oct 27, 2025: 'immediate with ... y^3 == y (mod 3)'). The statement file quotes this. The other conjecture in the entry (XOR formula) is not the one formalized.

oeis-a051195.note: Mathar's P-recurrence for the count of aperiodic binary words of length 2n+2 with n ones. The definition matches the data. By Moebius inversion a(n) = C(2n+2,n) - [n even] C(n+1,n/2), so the recurrence is a holonomic identity. Routine.

oeis-a052379.note: The entry records 'The conjecture is true' with a derivation (Vim Wenders, Mar 26 2008), and the statement file quotes it. Settled long before the PR.

oeis-a057300.note: Ralf Stephan's two recurrences for the base-4 digit swap 1<->2. The definition matches the data. A direct digit-level induction. Routine.

oeis-a081201.note: Hardin's conjecture: the number of collinear 6-sets in the 6^n grid is (8^n - 6^n)/2. A line meeting {0..5}^n in 6 points is a full tic-tac-toe winning line, and the classical Golomb-Hales count of winning lines on the k^n board is ((k+2)^n - k^n)/2. The PR re-proves a classical formula.

oeis-a085781.note: Mathar's P-recurrence for 2*C(2n+1,n+1) - 2^n, stated for n>=3. A routine holonomic verification.

oeis-a099576.note: The entry gives Robert Israel's closed forms (May 2018) followed by 'The conjecture follows from this', and the statement file says Israel resolved it. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a122648.note: The entry says 'Mathar's conjecture is true (see Fried link)' (Sela Fried, Dec 07 2025), and the statement file records this. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a132305.note: The statement matches Bala's 2025 supercongruence for sums of fifth powers of trinomial coefficients, a(np^k) == a(np^(k-1)) mod p^(2k), p>=5. oeis-a136433.note: Mathar's recurrence a(n) = 6a(n-3) + a(n-6) - 6a(n-9) for a linear recurrence with period-6 coefficients. The definition matches the data. A finite case split on n mod 6. Routine.

oeis-a163617.note: Yanev's identity a(n) = Gray(n) + (6n+1-(-1)^n)/4 (multiplied by 4). The definition is the unique solution on N and matches the data. Binary induction. Routine.

oeis-a167481.note: Mathar's P-recurrence for the convolution sum (-2)^{n-k} C(2k,k). A routine holonomic verification.

oeis-a191821.note: Dale's g.f. for an explicit closed form, with the offset-1 series handled correctly. A rational g.f. identity. Routine.

oeis-a192941.note: Mathar's recurrence for the constant term of (2x+1)...(2x+n) mod x^2-x-1. The definition matches the entry's examples. Routine.

oeis-a203233.note: The entry says the conjecture was '... verified by Robert Israel, May 04 2017', and the statement file says Israel verified it. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a233578.note: Kaarhus's criterion follows from von Staudt-Clausen. With m = den/6, num(B_n) == m (mod 6), and the sign of B_n (n mod 4) with 5 | m iff 4 | n gives exactly the residues {1,5,7,13,19} mod 30. Odd n are handled (B_n = 0). Routine.

oeis-a242992.note: The statement file says Oudra's conjecture was proved by Sela Fried (arXiv:2607.24832, Theorem 29). The entry says 'The conjecture is true (see Fried link)', Feb 2026. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a247339.note: Let p = spf(n^2+1) and m the least positive root of m^2 == -1 mod p. Then m <= n and m < p/2, so m^2+1 = p*c with c < p, hence gpf(m^2+1) = p (and p=2 gives m=1). This is the classical argument. The formalization is faithful. Routine.

oeis-a249067.note: The entry records 'The conjecture above is true. In fact, a(n) takes on precisely 37 values ... 81' (Charles R Greathouse IV, Mar 17 2018), quoted in the statement file. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a259714.note: Barker's recurrence and g.f. for a convolution recurrence with periodic weights (k mod 5). The definition matches the data. A rational g.f. identity. Routine.

oeis-a266251.note: Barker's closed form, recurrence and g.f. for the OFF cells of Rule 9, with the background evolving as in the entry's program and the data controls matching. The pattern becomes periodic, so this is a finite-structure induction. Routine.

oeis-a285383.note: Alex Ashburn, 'Proofs of some OEIS conjectures on Wythoff sums, Fibonacci and Lucas words' (arXiv:2610.04842, Oct 4 2026, linked from the entry), states 'we prove a conjecture of Mathar on A285383'. Settled before the PR (opened 2026-11-27).

oeis-a294515.note: This genuinely disproves Lang's conjecture a(n) = A250550(n+1)/(n+1), which is equivalent to gcd(n+1, num V(n)) = 1. The counterexample is n = 491244 = 19*25855 - 1, where 19 divides the numerator of V(n), established by a 19-adic block argument. My Python check found no failure for n < 400. The formal definitions match the data. A non-trivial counterexample.

oeis-a305503.note: The statement file says a 2026 Zenodo preprint claims a proof of Chu's conjecture a(n) = n-7. That record, 'Maximum Cardinality of MSTD Subsets of Integer Intervals', was published 2026-10-07 and says 'We prove this conjecture for every n>=16'. Chu (2020) had n-7 <= a(n) <= n-4. oeis-a326781.note: This disproves Barker's recurrence a(n) = a(n-1) + a(n-16) - a(n-17) at n=2049. a(2048)=32628 and a(2049)=65536, because bit 15 (position 16) is forbidden; I confirmed the first failures 2049, 2065, ... in Python. oeis-a329813.note: The statement makes Cicuttin's six-distinct-limits claim universal over ALL nonzero seeds (x,y). The entry gives the scaling law (C1 y, C2 y/x, C3/x, C4/y, C5 x/y, C6 x) 'for a generic seed', so special seeds trivially make two limits coincide. The disproof does exactly that (t = c1/c5 etc.). The proof file itself says the existence of the limits and the (1,1)-seed distinctness, the substantive open content, are not refuted.

oeis-a333794.note: Karttunen's conjecture (checked to 2^24) is that the gpf step is an optimal first step for the max path sum. The proof is a short exchange argument: for q < P = gpf(n), the q-step and P-step commute and gpf(n - n/q) = P, then strong induction. The formalization via fuelled recursion matches the data. Short but genuine.

oeis-a339532.note: Wu's recurrence and g.f. The Wieferich conditions for 2, 3, 5 are congruence conditions mod 4, 9, 25, so the set is a union of residue classes mod 900 minus b=1. That gives 8 terms per period, which is exactly the recurrence. Routine.

oeis-a353138.note: The fixed points of sum (#digits)^digit are only 1 and 4624. A bound (L <= 11 digits) plus an exhaustive kernel check over digit-count vectors. A finite check, routine.

oeis-a366860.note: The slope (sqrt(21)-3)/2 for the nested recurrence a(n) = n - a(floor(a(n-1)/3)). The formal statement includes the continued-fraction limit and the ratio limit. The proof uses strong induction with an O(sqrt n) error bound and a contraction of the two-level CF map. No earlier proof in the entry (revised Nov 9 2026). A modest but genuine analysis.

oeis-a372313.note: If A(n,1) == A(n,k-1) == 33 mod 100, their sum is 66 mod 100, so v2 = 1 and A372289 gives 2x+1 == 33 mod 100. A one-line induction. Trivial.

oeis-a374416.note: The statement matches 'a(n)=0 iff n=23' (practical number plus two nonagonal numbers k(7k-5)/2, k>=0). Somu-Tran (2024) proved representability only for sufficiently large n. The 129 KB proof gives an explicit construction at every scale (D q practical for D=2^t; nonagonal residues chosen mod D) plus kernel tables up to 8192. A complete, effective resolution; substantive.

oeis-a382465.note: Xausa's conjecture: A382462 (the lexicographically earliest stream with every even digit preceded by a smaller digit) is a permutation of A382465. The greedy encoding equals lexicographically earliest because a repunit always extends, so there are no dead ends. Each admissible number is eventually chosen because terms ending in 1 recur. A short argument.

oeis-a384270.note: Hanna's parity conjecture. The statement asserts existence of a normalized integer solution of A(x) A(x^3+3xA^3) = A(x^4+4xA^4) and, for every such solution, odd coefficients exactly at powers of 2. This matches the data (1,1,4,21,130). The proof is a char-2 analysis of the functional equation (27 KB). No earlier proof found. Moderate.

oeis-a390007.note: Rodrigo's uniqueness of the minimum-defect 3-rectangle Mondrian partition except n=4. The two normal forms (three strips, or one strip plus a perpendicular split) are justified, and the encoding identifies congruent sets correctly. The proof is an elementary case analysis over these families. No earlier proof found.

oeis-a400585.note: Kotesovec's sum_{k<=n} a(k) ~ 7 zeta(3) n^3/48 is immediate: sum over odd j of C(floor(n/j)+1,3) ~ (n^3/6)(7/8)zeta(3). Routine.

erdos-149.note: The statement requires a strong edge colouring as a total map Sym2 V -> Fin k with k <= (5/4)Delta^2. When Delta = 0 and V is nonempty this forces k = 0, and no map Sym2 V -> Fin 0 exists, because Sym2 V contains the diagonal elements. The disproof is exactly this: the empty graph on one vertex with Delta = 0. It says nothing about the Erdos-Nesetril conjecture, which is still open.

erdos-671.note: On the erdosproblems.com forum (22 Jun 2026), Liam Price posted that GPT Pro answers both questions of #671 in the affirmative, with a written argument and a Lean formalisation by Codex. The site's statement is the first question, and the proof builds an explicit node scheme. That is five months before PR #12324 (27 Nov 2026), so the result was already known.

Erdos338.erdos_338.variants.basis_after_.note: Shi-Qiang Chen, Quan-Hui Yang and Lilu Zhao, 'On a Problem of Erdos and Graham Related to Restricted Order' (arXiv:2611.33191, 15 Nov 2026), prove that if A minus F has finite order for every finite F, then A has a restricted order. mo-160389.note: Every combination of permutations of (a,b,c) has coordinate sum (sum of w)(a+b+c), so a constant vector (x,x,x) needs (a+b+c) | 3x. Hence the non-representable constants are unbounded unless a=b=c=1, and then there are none. A 2017 comment on the question already points out this obstruction. The disproof uses it with (1,1,3): 5k+1 is never representable. The result is routine and was already noted on MO.

mo-253925.note: Fedor Petrov answered the question affirmatively on 4 Nov 2016, splitting into three cases. If G_eps(x) is attained inside the interval, take h(x)=0. Otherwise use the one-sided derivative of G at x+eps or x-eps, together with the tangent-line inequality for a concave function. The formal statement (every concave G and eps >= 0 admit such h) matches the question. So this was settled on the source page years before the PR.

mo-280952.note: Ron Peretz answered on 12 Sep 2017 that C' = f(C) for convex games. The extreme points of the quotient core are marginal vectors (Shapley 1971), and each one is the image of a marginal vector of G for an order that keeps each union consecutive. The statement file itself says 'Status: this is a known result, not an open problem'.

mo-373182.note: The claim is the textbook fact that separability is transitive in towers, which is also in Mathlib. A comment on the question (3 Oct 2020) gives the proof: pass to the finite separable subextension generated by the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of a over L. The formal statement is faithful, but the result is routine and already answered on MO.

mo-452919.note: An MO answer (18 Aug 2023) gives a strongly connected 4-vertex digraph whose adjacency matrix has a 2x2 Jordan block at eigenvalue 0. The disproof formalises exactly that counterexample and credits the answer. The answer was already on the source page.

mo-487192.note: The MO post asks three separate questions. Q1 (poset centralisers semisimple) and Q2 (products of chains) are the substance, and Steinberg's comments essentially settle them positively via the transpose/C*-algebra argument. Q3 (any invertible matrix) is the one the asker says 'sounds wrong'. The statement (PR #9503, by the same contributor) bundles all three into a single conjunction. The statement PR openly plans to refute it through Q3, using a complex symmetric square-zero matrix. The disproof does exactly that, so the site shows the problem as disproved while Q1 and Q2 are true and untouched. The Q3 counterexample is standard: Steinberg's comment already notes that over C one needs A*, not A^T.

mse-2259412.note: The formal statement matches the source: infinitely many primes divide some 1!+...+n!. The MSE post has no answer. However, it is posed as a 'Prove that' exercise, and a comment links an older AoPS olympiad thread (c6h481900) with solution attempts. I could not load that thread (HTTP 403), so I cannot rule out a known solution. The proof uses a short elementary valuation argument at primes dividing n+2, and is plausibly the standard olympiad solution.

opg-a-transversal-achievement-game-on-a-.note: The statement file cites Randjelovic, 'The transversal game' (arXiv:2401.16768, v1 30 Jan 2024). That paper proves the first player wins the transversal achievement game for n >= 4, answering Erickson's question. The remaining cases n = 1, 2, 3 are finite checks, which the proof does by decide. So the result was known before the PR.

wpc-dixmier-unitarizability.note: The proof file says it is 'Adapted from OpenAI, openai/math@3344da5 ... This is a port, not an independent proof'. The statement file says its definitions come from openai/math lean/ComparatorChallenges/DixmierAllDiscrete.lean. The challenge and its solution modules have been in openai/math since its initial commit on 6 Oct 2026, so this is an earlier public proof.

mo-204379.note: The asker conjectured, from numerics, that the Jensen gap D(a;b) has a single maximum in a > 0. The formal statement asserts a unique global maximiser for any positive b that is not constant, with D defined exactly as in the question. The question (2015) has no answers, and the comments only discuss bounds. The proof writes D'(a) as a/(a+m)^3 times a weighted sum of strictly decreasing slope functions, so D' changes sign exactly once. This is a genuine (if elementary) argument, not a finite check.

oeis-a000254.note: These are Detlefs' four 2010 congruence conjectures for s(n+1,2). The entry says 'Detlefs' conjectures above and below are true (see Fried link). - Sela Fried, Oct 26 2025', and the statement file itself says 'all reported true by Sela Fried (2025)'. So they were settled a year before the PR.

oeis-a000657.note: Bala's May 2023 conjecture: median Euler numbers mod k are eventually periodic with period dividing phi(k). The Entringer-row definition reproduces the data (1,1,4,46,1024,36976,...), and the statement says exactly 'eventually periodic, period | phi(m)'. The entry still lists it as a conjecture, and I found no proof. The proof builds a finite-difference representation of the Entringer central values and applies Euler's theorem in each prime power. That takes a real idea, though the method is standard.

oeis-a002114.note: Bala's conjecture: Glaisher's H' mod k is eventually periodic with period dividing phi(k). The entry only notes the prime case (Bala, Oct 2026). The definition is the entry's finite-sum formula, which I checked against the data (1,11,301,15371,...); first>0 only skips the n=0 artefact. The proof is the standard argument: finite differences above the degree vanish, then Euler's theorem in each prime power. Routine given a formula already in the entry.

oeis-a003095.note: The entry's Bala conjectures (eventual period 2 mod 2^k, 6 mod 10^k and 6 mod 20^k) are headed 'Conjectures [added Jul 10 2026: see the Harden link for proofs]'. That link is David L. Harden, 'Proving the Bala conjectures'. So they were proved before the PR.

oeis-a005994.note: Mathar's 2025 conjecture a(n)+a(n+1) = A203286(n+1). I brute-forced the Configuration encoding (equal numbers of positive and negative entries, zero sum, at most n nonzero pairs), and it reproduces A203286 (4,12,28,57,...). The alkane formula reproduces A005994, and the identity checks for n <= 8. The proof is a bijective slice count. Routine.

oeis-a008705.note: Bala's 2023 supercongruences a(p) == -1-p and a(2p) == p-1 (mod p^2) for primes p >= 3, with a(n) = [x^n] Prod_{m<=n}(1-x^m)^n. The statement matches the entry, which still lists them as conjectures. The proof is a clean argument over ZMod(p^2) with 'good' polynomials whose coefficients at non-multiples of p are divisible by p. Short, but a genuine supercongruence proof.

oeis-a020964.note: Wu's Sep 2026 recurrence (n > 6) and g.f. The tsum definition with k+1 matches the entry (offset 0, data 1,4,11,28,...), and I checked that the recurrence holds for n >= 7 (it fails at n = 6, as the bound requires). The normalised g.f. reproduces the data. The proof shows the sum is finite and uses the silver-ratio trace recursion with a period-2 parity correction. A routine recurrence/g.f. identity.

oeis-a026019.note: This is Mathar's 2013 P-recurrence for C(3n,n) - C(3n,n-3). The entry now carries 'Conjecture verified using Maple's "simplify" command. - Robert Israel, Nov 24 2026' (revision of 25 Nov 2026). For a hypergeometric difference this is a proof. It predates PR #13201 (27 Nov), so the recurrence was already settled. It is a routine identity in any case.

oeis-a034108.note: Wu's 2024 recurrence (n > 8) and g.f. for the run starts of sqrt(m) whose first decimal is 2. The statement's digit and run-start encoding reproduces the data (5,18,28,39,...). I checked the recurrence and the g.f. for about 400 terms. The run starts are ceil((k+0.2)^2) for k = 2 and k >= 4, a quasi-polynomial of period 5. Routine.

oeis-a038867.note: Purath's conjecture that (n+5)^3 - n^3 is never a square. The statement is exact. The proof is one line: the value is 15n^2+75n+125, which is 2 mod 3, and squares are not. Trivial (the entry only reports a check up to 10^5). PR #7403 was the original proof; #7840 and #11167 shortened it.

oeis-a048331.note: Mathar's 2015 g.f. and recurrence a(n) = 7a(n-5) - 6a(n-10) for the base-6 repdigits, with a(0) = 0 included as in the entry. I checked the definition against the data and verified both identities numerically. The terms are d*(6^k-1)/5, so this is a routine g.f. identity.

oeis-a051397.note: This is Mathar's 2014 second-order recurrence. The entry itself says 'Mathar's conjectured recurrence ... follows easily from the defining recurrence', together with a continued-fraction consequence. The statement matches it, and the proof is two applications of the defining recurrence. Already settled in the entry and routine.

oeis-a054117.note: This is Mathar's 2013 recurrence a(n) - (n+1)a(n-1) + n a(n-2) = 0. The row-sum construction of A054115 reproduces the data (1,6,30,150,870,...). I checked that the recurrence holds for 5 <= n <= 19 and fails only at n = 4 (left side 4). The statement file says so and restricts to n >= 5, which is the usual 'sufficiently large n' reading of Mathar's recurrences. The proof is a short telescoping of the double sums. Routine.

oeis-a057923.note: This is Israel's 2017 conjecture a(n+2) > a(n) for the greedy sequence that makes the pairwise ORs strictly increasing. The pick/pair encoding reproduces all 63 data terms, and the claim holds for 300 terms. The proof is a 50-line bitwise argument (y + ldiff x y = y OR x). Routine. Git history is squashed; the PR number is the later of the two merged PRs titled oeis-a057923, and #6867 is presumably the statement.

oeis-a065796.note: Wilson's 2001 conjecture that infinitely many values are omitted. The entry already proves it: 'a(n) == n^2 (mod 11). In particular, values == 2, 6, 7, 8, 10 (mod 11) do not appear, and the conjecture is true. - Robert Israel, Oct 24 2017'. The statement file itself says 'Israel proved this ... We state the known conjecture'.

oeis-a071286.note: This is Barker's 2017 conjecture that the order-5 Peirce denominators are periodic with period 15 (the g.f. with denominator 1-x^15). I simulated the statement's token-stream insertion rule, and it reproduces the entry's data (2,4,5,3,1,5,4,3,5,4,2,5,3,4,5,...). The proof shows the insertion map preserves periodicity. This is the same routine pattern as A071284 in an earlier batch. Git history is squashed; the PR is the later of the two merged oeis-a071286 PRs.

oeis-a076035.note: This is Mathar's 2022 conjecture a(n) = 4*A076025(n). The entry says 'Mathar's conjecture is true (follows from the g.f.s of the two sequences). - Sela Fried, Dec 21 2025', and the statement file itself cites this. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a082143.note: This is Mathar's 2014 first-order recurrence (n+1)a(n) = 4(2n+1)a(n-1) for a(n) = 2^(n-1) C(2n+1,n). The definition matches the data. It holds for n >= 2; at n = 1 the 0^n/2 correction makes it fail, which the statement file notes. It is a one-line factorial identity. Routine.

oeis-a085799.note: The entry says: 'For n>=2, a(n) = (-1)^(n-1)*(n+1)/2*(2n-1)!/(n-2)!. Furthermore, the conjecture by Lajos is true (see Fried link). - Sela Fried, Feb 04 2026'. The statement file itself cites Theorem 5 and Corollary 1 of arXiv:2606.09913 for both parts. Known.

oeis-a088883.note: This is Rotondo's 2025 conjecture that every such prime is 1 mod 6. The statement's concatenation p*10^len(p) + rev(p) matches the entry's example (109 -> 109903). The proof is a mod-3 observation: rev(p) == p (mod 3), so concat(p,rev(p)) + 2 == 2(p+1) (mod 3), forcing p == 1 (mod 3); p = 2 and p = 3 fail directly. Trivial.

oeis-a094822.note: Both conjuncts are recorded as facts in the entry before the PR. Bala (Oct 27 2026) shows that Mathar's recurrence follows from A'/A = (9x-4)/(3x-1), and in the same block states that a(n) mod k is eventually periodic, as a result rather than a conjecture. The statement file says the same. The periodicity also follows at once from the integer recurrence by pigeonhole on (n mod k, a(n-1), a(n-2)). Known and routine.

oeis-a101917.note: The disproof refutes Stephan's g.f. (1+x^7)/(1+x+x^7) at coefficient 57. The entry already says 'this is wrong. This g.f. produces a sequence which differs at a(57) = -153367 ... - Johannes W. Meijer, Aug 08 2011', and the statement file cites this. Known since 2011.

oeis-a106252.note: Layman's conjecture that the first differences have period 6. The entry gives a(n) = n + floor(n/2) + floor(n/3) (Kimberling 2012), with the remark 'That the difference sequence ... is periodic follows from a formula in the Formula and Mathematica sections; see A211701'. So it was settled in 2012.

oeis-a112041.note: Dale's 2015 conjecture that every term other than the first (4) is a multiple of 10. The statement matches, and k = 4 is the first term. The proof is a residue check mod 2 and mod 5: k+1, 3k+1, 9k+1 and 27k+1 cover the nonzero residues mod 5 as k varies, so 5 | k unless one of them equals 5, which forces k = 4. Trivial.

oeis-a114948.note: The conjecture is that n^2 + 10 is never a perfect power. The entry says 'The conjecture is true: See Cohn. - James Rayman, Feb 14 2023', citing J. H. E. Cohn, Acta Arith. 65 (1993). The statement file and the proof both cite Cohn, and the proof formalises his argument in Z[sqrt(-10)]. Known since 1993.

oeis-a123341.note: Adams-Watters' 2006 conjecture that lim a(n)/2^n exists and is positive, where a(n) = sum_{k<=pi(n)} a(n-k). The definition reproduces the data (1,1,2,3,6,11,22,...). The entry and a web search show no proof. The proof shows that b(n) = a(n)/2^n satisfies b(n+1) >= b(n)(1 - 2^{-pi(n)}) and b(n+1) <= b(n). Since sum 2^{-pi(n)} converges (via a Chebyshev-type bound), the limit exists and is positive. Short, but a genuine analytic argument.

oeis-a127769.note: Mathar's 2014 recurrence for 3*C(4n-2,2n)/(2n+1), n > 1. The 'term' encoding is exactly a(k+1) = 3(4k+2)!/((2k+3)!(2k)!), and the recurrence is instantiated at n = t+2. The proof is field_simp and ring on factorials. A routine hypergeometric identity.

oeis-a133212.note: Mathar's 2007 conjecture a(n) = 2*A038503(n+3) for n > 0, where A038503(n) = sum_k C(n,4k). The recurrence and the binomial sum match both entries. The identity holds for n = 1..39 and fails at n = 0, as the statement notes. The proof is a binomial-transform argument with a 4-periodic indicator. A routine linear-recurrence identity.

oeis-a141351.note: Mathar's 2014 P-recurrence for Catalan(n) + 1 - 0^n. The statement restricts to n >= 4 because at n = 3 the 0^n correction gives left side 2, which I confirmed. The recurrence holds for n = 4..39. The proof uses (j+2)C(j+1) = 2(2j+1)C(j) and ring. A routine identity.

oeis-a155559.note: Curtz's conjecture a(n) = A090129(n+3) - A090129(n+2), where A090129(n) is the order of 3 mod 2^n. A090129 records that this order is 2^(n-2) for n >= 3, with a proof link. Given that, the conjecture is immediate: 2^(n+1) - 2^n = 2^n = a(n), and n = 0 gives 2 - 2 = 0. Settled by a classical fact already in the OEIS, as with A002050 in an earlier batch. Git history is squashed; the PR is the later merged oeis-a155559 PR.

oeis-a164008.note: Mathar's 2010 conjecture: row 8 of A163280 equals n(n+7) for n > 9. I recomputed the array from the statement's lowerDiv/Nat.nth encoding. It reproduces the data (0,17,34,39,68,65,102,98,...) and n(n+7) holds for 10 <= n < 190. The proof characterises the small elements of each column. Elementary and routine.

oeis-a167493.note: The disproof refutes Shevelev's conjecture 1 (every difference is 1 or prime) at n = 620757, where the difference is 27. The entry already records this counterexample: 'Conjecture #1 above fails at n = 620757, with a(n) = 1241487 and a(n-1) = 1241460, difference = 27. - Bill McEachen, Jan 20 2023'. The proof checks it by kernel evaluation and credits McEachen. Known since 2023.

oeis-a175784.note: Mathar's 2010 conjectures: a(n) = 4*A060791(n+2), a(n) = 2a(n-5) - a(n-10), and the g.f. All three are stated, with the reduced-numerator definition (data 12,16,4,24,...), and I checked all three numerically. Since (2n-1)/(2n+9) + 1 = 4(n+2)/(2n+9) and gcd(4(n+2), 2n+9) = gcd(n+2, 5), everything follows from 5-periodicity. Routine.

oeis-a178299.note: Mathar's 2010 closed form a(n) = 3*8^n + 3*10^n/2 - 5*6^n + 12^n/2 for collinear 4-point subsets of {0..5}^n. The Finset/Collinear encoding counts unordered 4-sets, matching a(1) = 15 = C(6,4), a(2) = 234 and a(3) = 2820. The 1200-line proof is a standard double count: a collinear 4-set has step 3, 4 or 5 along its line, with a 2-to-1 parameterisation. Long, but routine combinatorics. I found no earlier proof.

oeis-a182208.note: Coman's 2012 conjecture that every Carmichael number divisible by 7 has the form 7(6m+1)(6n+1) or 7(6m-1)(6n-1). The entry says 'The conjecture follows from Korselt's criterion. - Charles R Greathouse IV, Oct 02 2012', and the statement file itself says 'This is a known result'.

oeis-a185010.note: This is Mathar's 2016 P-recurrence for Catalan(n)*A015518(n+1). The entry links Ekhad and Yang (2017), 'Proofs of Linear Recurrences of Coefficients of Certain Algebraic Formal Power Series Conjectured in the OEIS'. Its Theorem 27 is exactly this recurrence for A185010, from the algebraic g.f. (2-8x-2 sqrt(1-8x-48x^2))^(1/2)/(8x). So it was proved in 2017. The formalisation itself is faithful (I checked the definitions against the data).

oeis-a191993.note: Mathar's 2017 P-recurrence for 3^(n-1) + C(2n,n)/2, instantiated at n = t+3. Over Q the definition matches the data (2,6,19,62,207,...), and the recurrence holds for n >= 3. The proof is the central-binomial step and ring. Routine.

oeis-a192745.note: Mathar's 2014 recurrence for the x-coefficient of p(n,x) mod x^2-x-1, where p(n,x) = x p(n-1,x) + n!. The modByMonic encoding reproduces the data (0,1,2,5,13,42,175,...), and the recurrence holds for n = 3..29. The proof shows the combination is a multiple of x^2-x-1 plus a constant. Routine.

oeis-a192942.note: Mathar's 2014 recurrence for the x-coefficient of (2x+1)...(2x+n) mod x^2-x-1. The encoding reproduces the data (0,2,10,62,448,...), and the recurrence holds for n = 2..29. The proof tracks the 2-dimensional coordinates of the reduction and eliminates one of them. Routine.

oeis-a199705.note: Barker's 2018 g.f. and parity closed forms for zero-sum triples in -n..n with no equal neighbours. The Finset filter reproduces the data (6,14,32,52,82,...), and both parity formulas and the g.f. check numerically. The proof counts fibres over the middle entry. Routine.

oeis-a203242.note: Mathar's 2013 P-recurrence and Barker's empirical g.f. The entry has a block 'From Robert Israel, Feb 01 2019: ... Conjecture and empirical g.f. verified.', and the statement file says 'Robert Israel verified both in 2019'. Settled before the PR.

oeis-a218755.note: Curtz's conjecture that the differences of Bernoulli denominators == 6 (mod 9) are multiples of 36. The entry says 'The conjecture is true, since elements of A090801 are 2 mod 4. - Charles R Greathouse IV, Nov 22 2012', and the statement file quotes this. The proof formalises Greathouse's argument via von Staudt-Clausen. Known since 2012.

oeis-a227721.note: Kimberling's 2013 conjecture floor(1/s(n)) = 6n^2+9n+2 (plus the induced cubic recurrence), with s(n) = (2n+1)/(2n+2) - n log((n+1)/n). The definition matches the entry, and I checked the closed form in 60-digit arithmetic for n < 300. The proof brackets log(1+1/n) with the atanh series in y = 1/(2n+1), showing 1/s(n) lies in [6n^2+9n+2, 6n^2+9n+3). Standard series estimates, so routine.

oeis-a233579.note: Kaarhus's 2013 conjecture: den(B_n)/6 mod 30 is in {11,17,23,25,29} iff |num(B_n)| == 5 (mod 6). The statement covers all n, and odd n and n <= 1 are handled correctly. I checked the equivalence for n <= 260 with exact Bernoulli numbers. It follows from von Staudt-Clausen: num == -den/2 (mod 2) and -den/3 (mod 3), and the sign of B_2k is tied to whether 5 | den. A short consequence of classical theorems. Routine.

oeis-a243513.note: Barker's 2018 closed form 4a(n) = 7 + 3^n + 2n and g.f. for Hardin's restricted-growth words avoiding aba/abb. The validWord encoding (each nonzero value preceded by its predecessor; consecutive-triple condition) is the restricted-growth condition. A brute force for n <= 6 reproduces the data and the formula. The proof splits by maximum value. Routine.

oeis-a248183.note: Oudra's 2023 conjecture a(n) = floor(sqrt(n^2/2+1) - 1/2) for n > 1, stated with the equivalent integer square root form (isqrt(2n^2+4)-1)/2. The tail telescopes to 1/(2(k+1)(k+2)), so the claim is a quadratic inequality. I checked it by brute force for n < 120. Routine.

oeis-a253975.note: Ratushnyak's 2015 conjecture that no term is -1, i.e. for every n some k has exactly n representations x*y+x+y with x >= y > 1. The statement (Fin n equivalent to the representations of k) is that existence claim. The proof takes k = 3^(2n+1) - 1: then (x+1)(y+1) = 3^(2n+1) has exactly n factorisations with y+1 = 3^j, 1 <= j <= n. Trivial.

oeis-a259775.note: Mathar's 2015 P-recurrence for the stepped path through iterated partial sums of squares. The partialSums/path encoding reproduces the data (1,5,6,20,27,77,112,...), and the recurrence (at n = t+4) checks exactly for 26 shifts. The proof finds the closed form (2j+r+2)(j+r+1)!/((r+2)! j!) and verifies a rational identity. Routine.

oeis-a262999.note: Sun's 2015 conjecture says a(n) = 1 only for n in {3,5,7,35,37,217,7439,10381}. The statement adds 590, because the entry's own example has a(590) = 1. That weakens the claim, so a disproof of it refutes Sun's version too. The disproof shows a(7872413) = 1 with the single pair (15015, 4749). I reproduced this with an independent numpy sieve to 1.39e8: pi(112732620) = 6450605, pi(22553001) = 1421808, and exactly one representation. Sun had checked only to 120000, and I found no earlier report. A computational counterexample, so routine.

oeis-a266438.note: De Vlieger's g.f. and Barker's closed form and recurrence for the cumulative ON cells of Rule 23. The background evolves as in the entry's program, which I simulated: it reproduces the data (1,4,4,11,11,22,...) and both formulas for n <= 40. The proof uses the rule 'ON iff at most one neighbour is ON', which gives an eventually periodic pattern. Routine, like the other Barker CA items in earlier batches.

oeis-a266795.note: Barker's closed form (n > 3), recurrence (n > 8) and g.f. for the cumulative OFF cells of Rule 61, with the background evolving. My simulation reproduces the data (0,1,4,6,11,15,23,...) and both formulas in their stated ranges. An eventually periodic CA pattern. Routine.

oeis-a267514.note: The disproof refutes Barker's 2016 recurrence and g.f. for the Rule 137 centre column at n = 62. The entry already says 'This conjectured linear recurrence fails to predict the correct values from a(62) on. - R. J. Mathar, Apr 12 2019', and the statement and proof files both cite this. Known since 2019.

oeis-a267923.note: Barker's recurrence a(n) = 101a(n-1) - 100a(n-2) (n > 2) and g.f. for the Rule 245 rows read in base 10. The background evolves (000 -> ON) as in the entry's program, which I simulated: it gives 1, 11, 11011, 1111011, ..., and the recurrence holds for n = 3..30. The proof shows row n is ON everywhere except cell n-2. Routine.

oeis-a276646.note: Krizek's 2016 conjecture that (sum_{k<=n} 0.k)/n <= 0.55. The exact decimalFraction k/10^(len k) is the source's 0.k. In exact arithmetic the mean stays below 0.55 up to n = 2*10^5, approaching it at n = 10^d - 1 (0.549977...). The proof is an elementary block-by-block arithmetic-progression bound. Routine. Git history is squashed; the PR is the later merged oeis-a276646 PR.

oeis-a285802.note: Lowell's conjecture that 35 is the largest value. The entry gives a full proof: 'Conjecture is true. ... a(10k) = a(k) ... for any k between 1 and 99 not ending in 0 there is a multiple not larger than 35k which has a 7 in one of its last two digits ... - Giovanni Resta, Apr 27 2017'. The statement file quotes this. Known since 2017.

oeis-a295432.note: Bala's conjecture that 6(6n+1)(12n-1) divides A295432(n). The entry (rev. 20 Nov 2026) links Miguel Cerda Bennassar, 'Divisibility of Two Integral Factorial Ratios by Linear Forms: Proofs of Conjectures of Bala' (Zenodo, published 6 Nov 2026). Its abstract says all of Bala's divisibility conjectures for A295431/A295432 are proved, via a Legendre-formula criterion, the same method as the Lean proof. That was three weeks before PR #10178.

oeis-a306571.note: The disproof refutes Sun's 2019 conjecture that every n is w(w+1) + C(x+3,4) + C(y+5,6) + C(z+7,8). The counterexample is n = 41215718, which has no representation. Sun had checked n up to 2*10^7. I confirmed with an independent brute force that a(41215718) = 0, a(41215717) = 15 and a(41215719) = 44, as the certificate states. The definition reproduces the 101 data terms. I found no earlier report of this counterexample. A computational disproof (finite check), so routine, but a genuine new refutation.

oeis-a327136.note: Kimberling's comment claims 1.285 < n*Pi - a(n) < 1.286 for n >= 1. The entry's own data contradicts it at once: a(1) = 1 gives Pi - 1 = 2.14, and n*Pi - a(n) runs through 2.14, 2.28, 1.42, 1.57, ... The statement transcribes the comment faithfully, and the disproof is exactly this n = 1 failure. The comment is false on the entry's own data (probably a typo). Nothing new, and arguably it should not count as a solved open problem.

oeis-a330080.note: Cicuttin's 2019 conjecture 0 <= floor(b(n)) <= 5 for b(n) = (b(n-1)+b(n-2))/b(n-3) with b(1) = b(2) = b(3) = 1. The proof uses the conserved quantity (1+x)(1+y)(1+z)(x+y+z)/(xyz) = 24 of this third-order Lyness-type map, which is classical (Cima-Gasull-Manosa), and a polynomial inequality showing every term is below 6. No proof is in the entry. Routine given the known invariant.

oeis-a334337.note: Sun's 2020 conjecture that for every n some m makes phi(mn) a cube; the second conjunct is the trivially true implication from A259915. The proof is the classical trick. With F = n!, every prime dividing phi(F) divides F, so phi(F*phi(F)^j) = phi(F)^(j+1). Take j = 2. Faithful, but trivial. I found no explicit earlier record for this entry.

oeis-a344598.note: Bala's 2024 conjecture a(n) = sum_{k=1..2n} (-1)^k gcd(k,4n). The entry already has Weber's proved formula a(n) = sum_{d|n} phi(d)(2n/d - 1) (MO 2026), but not Bala's form. The proof pairs the terms of the alternating gcd sum and reduces it to Weber's divisor sum. A routine consequence of a formula already in the entry.

oeis-a355175.note: Sun's 2022 closed form for det[(i-j)^2 + delta_ij]. The entry says 'The conjecture is true (see Fried link). - Sela Fried, Feb 01 2026', and the statement file cites Fried, Section 3.9 of arXiv:2606.09913. Known.

oeis-a366870.note: Gutkovskiy's 2023 conjecture a(n) ~ 2(sqrt 2 - 1) n for a(n) = n - a(floor(a(n-1)/4)), a Hofstadter-G variant. The definition and the continued-fraction limit match the entry. The entry and its siblings (denominators 3 and 5) still list it as a conjecture, and I found no proof. The proof bounds the error from the linear slope by 16 sqrt(n) by strong induction, for any denominator >= 3, using contraction of the two-level continued-fraction map. A genuine asymptotic argument.

oeis-a372430.note: The disproof refutes Wiseman's 2024 conjecture that 4100 is the only k whose binary indices are a subset of its prime indices (verified only to 10^7). The counterexample is k = 2^87 + 2^49 = 154742504911235484315811840. Its binary indices are {50, 88}, and I checked that prime(50) = 229 and prime(88) = 457 both divide it. The encoding (1-based bit positions, prime(1) = 2) matches the entry's example 4100. No earlier report found. An explicit computational counterexample, so routine, but a genuine new refutation.

oeis-a375583.note: The conjecture (checked to 10^8) is that 11 is the only n that is not a practical number plus two 11-gonal numbers. Somu-Tran (JIS 2024, Thm 2) prove this only for n > N(s), with an astronomically large, never-computed N(s), so the conjecture was open. The definitions (practical number; k(9k-7)/2, k >= 0) are faithful. The 900-line proof gives an explicit construction at every scale: Dq is practical for D = 2^t and q <= 2D, and the polygonal residues are chosen mod D = BL, plus a finite check. A substantive effectivisation. Git history is squashed; the PR is the later merged oeis-a375583 PR.

oeis-a382624.note: Xausa's 2025 conjecture that A382621 (lexicographically earliest digit-stream sequence) sorted is A382624. The greedy state with seed 9 and the least-unused rule reproduce A382621's opening (1,3,2,5,4,7,6,9,8,10,...). The statement says this sequence is injective with image exactly the admissible numbers. The proof uses that all-nines repunits can follow anything, so every admissible number is eventually used. Routine.

oeis-a386580.note: Wiseman's 2025 conjecture that the multisets with a distinct-run-length permutation are equinumerous with those admitting disjoint strict partitions of their multiplicities. The Composition/splitBy encoding is faithful. A brute force for n <= 12 reproduces the data (1,1,1,3,3,5,12,13,20,27,64,71,108), and the two properties agree composition by composition. The proof shows this per-multiset equivalence by merging blocks of an overrepresented letter and then arranging blocks with distinct letters at each boundary. Elementary but a real combinatorial argument.

oeis-a390815.note: Dequatre's two Feb 2026 conjectures: every reduced denominator > 1 of n!/sigma(n) is prime, and for n >= 4, sigma(n) not dividing n! forces n to be a square. Both are stated faithfully. The proof is elementary. If n is not a prime power, sigma(n) | n! by multiplicativity. If n = p^k, sigma(n) < 2n, so it divides n! or is a prime > n, and for odd k, (1+p) | sigma(n) rules the latter out. Routine.

oeis-a301517.note: Lagneau's 2018 conjecture: if (sum of nonsquarefree divisors)/(sum of squarefree divisors) is a perfect square, it is the square of a prime. PR #7662 disproved it with root 3107; the merged file (#10580) uses n = 19773000 = 2^3*3^2*5^3*13^3, where I recomputed the sums 1008 and 72398592, ratio 71824 = 268^2 with 268 composite. oeis-a330408.note: Sada's conjecture that the diagonal of the least-multiple table is A166447 = n*round(sqrt n). The table definition reproduces the entry's antidiagonals. I recomputed A(19,19) = 95 (19 -> 20 -> 21 -> 24 -> 25 -> 30 -> ... -> 95) against A166447(19) = 76, so the claim first fails at n = 19. The entry has no earlier correction. A finite counterexample.

oeis-a334765.note: Konig's 2020 conjecture: no four consecutive terms (binary weight = minus the balanced-ternary digit sum). The extra conjuncts restate the comment's data (first run 32770..32772, 115 earlier terms) and are finite checks. The core is a short parity argument. For n not 1 mod 3 the ternary sum goes up by 1, so the binary weight must drop by 1, which forces n = 3 mod 4. Two of three consecutive n would both need this, which is impossible. Not in the entry.

oeis-a000267.note: Karttunen's conjecture A070939(A227368(n+1)) = floor(sqrt(4n+1)). I checked that the formal run-length decoder reproduces A227183 and its first-occurrence codes reproduce A227368, and that the identity holds for n<60. The proof is an elementary extremal argument: the largest partition encodable in L bits has size floor((L+1)^2/4), from balanced rectangles. Not settled in the entry.

oeis-a026741.note: Hopper's lcm(n,p) = p*a(n,p) and gcd(n,p) = n/a(n,p) for prime p, where a(n,p) = n/p if p|n and n otherwise. Faithful for n>0. A two-case triviality.

oeis-a058764.note: Hasler's conjecture: the least x with x - phi(x) = 2^n is 3*2^(n-1) for n>1. The entry gives only the upper bound (Mathar). The proof writes x = 2^a m and shows that 2m - phi(m) can be a power of 2 with m>1 only when phi(m) is 2 mod 4. That makes m a prime power p^k with p = 3 mod 4, so phi(m)/m >= 2/3. A short elementary argument.

oeis-a076902.note: Cloitre's |a(n) - n/3| < log(n+1) plus a(n) ~ n/3. The definition matches the data (checked). With e(n) = a(n) - n/3, |e(n)| <= 1/3 + |e(n/2)|, so |e(n)| <= (1/3)log2(n) + O(1), well below ln(n+1). Routine.

oeis-a108475.note: Mathar's a(n) = Pell(n+1)*A001333(n) for the coefficients of (1-3x)/(1-5x-5x^2+x^3). The definitions match the data (checked). A product of two C-finite sequences: a routine identity (10-line proof).

oeis-a127771.note: Barry's conjecture that the inverse of the triangle 1/phi(n+1)[k<=n<=2k] is integral, stated for every finite truncation (equivalent). oeis-a134347.note: Werner's closed form for the inverse binomial transform of A134346(n,k) = (2^(n+1)-1)C(n,k). The definitions reproduce the data (checked). A routine binomial-sum identity.
